diagnostic_evidence.quote: Provided $T$ is small enough, {we obtain the (uniform in $\eta$) boundedness of $h_{0,x}^{\eps,{\eta}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The circular argument for (holder-space-gamma) and (holder-space-gammah) closes only if C·T^{(α-1)/α} < 1, so it works only for small T. The proposition and Theorem 1 are stated for arbitrary T with constants depending on T. The 'w.l.o.g. T small' is not justified. Passing to general T needs an extra chaining argument (Chapman–Kolmogorov from intermediate times, restarting the estimates), and for the scheme this must be done on the grid with the h^{1/α} correction.

failure_location.quote: Since $ \gamma-\beta=\alpha-1>0$, Equation \eqref{holder-space-gammah} then follows taking the supremum in time in the previous inequality provided $T $ is small enough.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a standard semigroup/chaining step: apply the small-time estimate on windows of length at most T_0 started at intermediate times, and combine with the Aronson bounds and Chapman–Kolmogorov for the rest.
issues.overall_effect: The Hölder controls, and hence the cancellation lemmas and the main theorem, are rigorously established only for T below a threshold.
issues.title: Spatial Hölder estimates proved only for small T; extension to arbitrary T not argued
issues.why_classification: The fix is a standard, contained iteration that preserves all statements and rates, with no new global architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: For t in (h,2h) the integrals over [h, τ_t^h-h] are empty or reversed. Δ_6 then runs over [0,t] and overlaps Δ_1. Its estimate uses (1+(τ_s^h)^{-β/α}), which is infinite when τ_s^h=0, where Γ^h(0,x,τ_s^h,·) is a Dirac mass and the Hölder cancellation is meaningless. The case t<2h is not treated separately. The bound required there, of order h^{(α-1)/α}·p̄, is not covered by the trivial bound |Γ^h-Γ| ≲ p̄.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Treat t≤2h directly via the Duhamel formulas, |Γ^h-Γ| ≲ ∫_0^t (t-s)^{-1/α} ds · p̄ ≲ t^{1-1/α} p̄ ≲ h^{γ/α} t^{-β/α} p̄ (using t ≲ h), and run the decomposition only for t≥2h.
issues.overall_effect: The estimate (BD_THM) is not proved for t<2h. This is where the factor t^{-β/α} matters most.
issues.title: Small-time regime t<2h not covered by the decomposition
issues.why_classification: A short direct estimate fixes the degenerate regime without changing method or rate.

issues.failure_explanation: ∫_h^t s^{-γ/α}(t-s)^{-1/α} ds is of order t^{1-(γ+1)/α} = t^{-β/α} (Beta integral), which is unbounded as t→0. The claimed bound without a factor t^{-β/α} is therefore false for small t.
issues.overall_effect: Only the displayed intermediate bound is wrong. The final gathered bound already carries (1+t^{-β/α}), so the theorem is unaffected.
issues.title: Δ_2 estimate drops the time-singularity factor t^{-β/α}
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction that the final statement already absorbs; no claim is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The scheme term in Δ_6 is E[b(U,X^h_{τ_s})∇_y p(t-s,y-X^h_s)]. Since X^h_s = X^h_{τ_s}+b(U,X^h_{τ_s})(s-τ_s)+Z_s-Z_{τ_s}, this equals ∫Γ^h b ∇p(t-τ_s, y-z-b(r,z)(s-τ_s)) dz, as the paper itself writes for Δ_322. Δ_62 instead uses ∇p(t-s,y-z), ignoring both the drift displacement and the shift t-s→t-τ_s. In the last step, where t-s may be smaller than h^α, the displacement is not negligible. The invoked bounds (USEFUL_FOR_DELTA_6) and (drift-smoothing-iso-noise) are therefore applied to the wrong integrand.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite Δ_62 with the correct conditional expectation and treat it as Δ_322/Δ_43 are treated (pivot at y-b(r,y)(s-τ_s), Taylor expansion, Lemma THE_LEMMA_FOR_SCHEME). Check that the resulting terms are O(h^{γ/α}).
issues.overall_effect: The bound (maj-D6-mainthm) for the last time step is not established as written. The final theorem is unaffected only if the repair succeeds.
issues.title: Scheme part of Δ_6 written with the wrong expectation (drift displacement and time shift ignored)
issues.why_classification: This needs a contained extra pivot/Taylor argument, parallel to existing ones, with no change of rate or method.

issues.failure_explanation: Δ_3 is defined with ∇_y p(t-s,·) and integrated over [h, τ_t^h-h]. The Gronwall inequality is written with ∇_y p(t-τ_s^h,·) over [h,t]. The differences, namely a time shift in the kernel for both the diffusion and the scheme terms and the tail interval [τ_t^h-h,t], are neither estimated nor assigned to Δ_4, Δ_5 or Δ_6. Δ_42 treats only the scheme piece. The diffusion piece, with the density Γ, and the shift for X_{τ_s}^h inside Δ_3 need their own cancellation estimates.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing estimates for the time-shift terms (diffusion and scheme) on [h,t/2], [t/2,τ_t^h-h] and the tail, using the same cancellation and time-Taylor arguments as for Δ_42, and then close the Gronwall argument.
issues.overall_effect: The inequality for f(t) that feeds the Volterra–Gronwall lemma is not justified as written, so the conclusion of the theorem rests on an unproved step.
issues.title: Gronwall step silently replaces t-s by t-τ_s in Δ_3 and enlarges the integration range
issues.why_classification: It needs additional estimates by existing techniques, with no change of the rate or architecture.
